notes:
The page continues a sentence about exterior profinite groups with Γ actions. It suggests that theorem 3 of the preceding section, applied to a suitably punctured projective line, could provide a construction. The second paragraph argues heuristically that arbitrary exterior homomorphisms lack geometric meaning, while commutation with the very restrictive Γ action should force geometric origin through field embeddings. It stresses a base such as Q or a finite-type extension and then restricts to homomorphisms with open image; the page ends in the unfinished word sequence ouverte — sinon. No author page number is visible. Thin foliation 41 is at bottom left and remains a margin item. The single top insertion profinis is attached between groupes and extérieurs by a curved leader. The one cancelled short word after Bien remains uncertain. The sheet has no display, drawing, or diagram. Operations has a final s; no quotation marks surround appliqué; three dots follow troué. The first π-map decorations remain genuinely ambiguous between bar and wedge-like overwritten forms, while the map arrow itself has a clear head. M1095 is resolved in the blind audit to n’auront, on the separate o and nt strokes; this is the listed alternative to C’s first n’auraient. M1096 resolves to Donc, M1097 to literal =. Both hom abbreviations are dotless in the ink, independently checked. The final π-map is headless, and the curve after sinon is joined to n rather than a detached comma. The low base-field k is read under the recurring notation reported by the main reader, as detailed in the hand log; this is recognition of an ambiguous habitual letter, not correction of a clear h. No mathematical proof or independent research was undertaken. Audit readings are contiguous target text with actual source punctuation, not summaries or editorial ellipses.

[Blind audit] A direct hat-on-K interpretation is added to the already unresolved upper decorations of the full pi map. The pi forms have the same curved top return and short oblique legs as the nearby lower-case kernel notation; no capital substitution is made solely from their three-stroke skeleton. The cancelled word after Bien now admits en/sur. The physical line break in manifeste-/ment has a separately written hyphen, retained as manifeste-ment in the reflowed fragment and explicitly treated as line division, not a spelling claim. Décrète has the visible d, accented e, c/r, accented e, t and final e; no new doubt is needed. The final sinon curve belongs to n and is not a comma. No mathematical check was undertaken.
